extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants/agents, patent owners and patent examiners in Korea (especially pharmaceutical and agrochemical industries)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for applying for and examining patent term extensions under Korean law (extensions due to regulatory approvals for drugs, veterinary drugs, agrochemicals and raw agrochemical materials). Covers eligibility, calculation of extension period, required documents, filing periods, representation, and examination procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible subject matter for extension
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensions are limited to: ① inventions of medicines (limited to medicines produced with the new matter whose chemical structure of the active part with medicinal effect is the active ingredient and is obtained with approval for items) subject to approval under Article 31(2) or (3) or 42(1) of the Pharmaceutical Affairs Act; and ② inventions of agricultural chemicals or raw materials (limited to those produced with the new matter as the active ingredient and registered for the first time) to be registered under Articles 8(1), 16(1), 17(1) of the Agrochemicals Control Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These inventions are limited to ones that have not been practiced for a certain period to obtain approval/registration. Other inventions, even if not practiced before obtaining approval/registration under other Acts, are not subject to extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent right must be valid at time of filing
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for registration of an extension can be filed only when the right of a patented invention is still valid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the patent has been invalidated, cancelled, or extinguished for failure to pay fees, the application is not recognized as valid. If an invalidation trial is pending, an application can be filed. If the patent was valid at filing but later invalidated/cancelled, the examiner must give the applicant an opportunity to explain under Article 11 of the Enforcement Rules and, if not addressed, return the written application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice when multiple approvals for multiple active ingredients in one patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Where multiple approvals are made on multiple active ingredients disclosed in a single patent, an applicant may choose only one permitted ingredient and apply for a one-time extension for that ingredient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: active ingredients A, B and C in one patent with three separate approvals — applicant may file for extension for only one chosen ingredient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Only initial approval counts for multiple approvals of same ingredient
rubrics_metrics.description: Where multiple approvals are made on the same active ingredient disclosed in a single patent, extension can be filed only on the initial approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: if Product Approval A (initial), API Approval B, and Dosage Change C were obtained consecutively for the same ingredient, the application for extension may be filed using the initial approval A only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple patents related to a single approval each can be extended
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a single approval is associated with multiple patents (e.g., product, process, use patents) that are necessary to practice the patented invention, extensions for the term of each patented invention may be filed separately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Approval D for an API that is covered by Patent A (product), Patent B (process) and Patent C (use) — extensions can be filed for each patent separately if approval is necessary to practice each.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum extension period is five years
rubrics_metrics.description: The term of a patent right may be extended by a period up to five years during which the patented invention could not have been practiced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if more than five years elapsed to obtain approval/registration, extension cannot exceed five years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation window for extension period (general rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Only the period elapsed after the date of registration of the patent right is considered for calculation of the period during which the invention could not be practiced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elapsed periods attributable to the holder/applicant during review of application documents at the approval/registration office are excluded from the calculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation components — human drugs (KFDA/KFDA)
rubrics_metrics.description: For drugs (excluding veterinary drugs), the extension calculation includes: the total length of the period for clinical trials conducted after obtaining approval from the Commissioner of the Korean Food and Drug Administration and the period for reviewing relevant documents for the application for approval elapsed at the Korean Food and Drug Administration to obtain items license of drugs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clinical trial and regulatory review periods at the relevant approval authority are counted; applicant-caused delays at the authority's document review that are attributable to the applicant are excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation components — veterinary drugs
rubrics_metrics.description: For veterinary drugs, the calculation includes the total length of the period for clinical trials conducted after obtaining approval from the Commissioner of the Animal, Plant and Fisheries Quarantine and Inspection Agency and the period for reviewing relevant documents for the application for approval elapsed at that Agency to obtain items license of veterinary drugs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same principles on excluding applicant-attributable review delays apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation components — agrochemicals and raw agrochemical materials
rubrics_metrics.description: For agrochemicals, the calculation includes: the total length of period for clinical trials conducted by test and research institutes designated under the Enforcement Decree of the Agrochemicals Control Act and the period for reviewing relevant documents for the application for approval elapsed at the Rural Development Administration to obtain registration of agrochemicals or active ingredients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For raw agrochemical materials, include test/analysis application periods and registration review periods as evidenced in filings and certificates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application content required (Article 90(1) items)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application must state: 1) name and domicile of applicant (or corporation name/place of business); 2) name and domicile/place of business of agent if represented; 3) patent number and indication of the claims to be extended; 4) the length of extension applied; 5) details of approval etc. under Article 89(1); 6) the ground for extension as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry (accompanied by substantiating materials).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All items must be stated in the application; omissions or incorrect statements can lead to formal rejection or requirement to amend.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing deadline for application
rubrics_metrics.description: An application must be filed within three months from the date when approval, etc. is received under Article 89(1); however, no application may be filed within six months prior to the expiration date of the patent term under Article 88.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an application was filed before approval was obtained, if more than three months elapsed from approval date, during the period between six months before patent expiration and the patent expiry, or after expiry, an examiner shall give opportunity to explain under Article 11 and may return the application if not addressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant must be patent holder (or all co-owners jointly)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant of registration for patent term extension is limited to the holder of the patent right; where the patent is jointly owned, application shall be made in the names of all co-owners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the filer is not the patent right holder or the application is not filed in names of all joint owners, this constitutes ground for rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of filing — provisional extension status
rubrics_metrics.description: When an application to register an extension of a patent is filed, the term shall be deemed extended: provided, however, that this does not apply where a decision to reject the application becomes final and conclusive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If application is withdrawn, invalidated or returned before a final decision to reject is conclusive, the term is deemed not to have been extended. A decision to reject becomes final when 30 days have elapsed from service of certified copy of rejection if no appeal was initiated; if appealed, finality follows appeal decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment rights and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may amend matters 3 through 6 (claims, length of extension, details of approval, grounds substantiating extension) stated in the application before the Commissioner serves a certified copy of decision of rejection; if a notice of ground for rejection has been served, amendments are allowed only during the period set for submission of written arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments after that period are restricted; legitimacy of amendments will be assessed during substantive examination (see rules on which amended application becomes subject for examination).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required evidential documents to attach
rubrics_metrics.description: Attach 'a copy of the evidential document of the ground for extension' and 'a copy of the evidential document of representation' (if represented) to the application (Annexed Form No.30).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: For drugs, include copy of clinical investigation plans, copy of items license for drugs, evidential document of Phase III trial period conducted overseas and review period at approval agency. For agrochemicals include test application for registration and registration certificate. For raw agrochemical materials include test and analysis applications and registration certificates.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to complete specific fields in the application form
rubrics_metrics.description: Fields to be filled: applicant name(s); patent number and application number; name of the patented invention; all claims including active pharmaceutical ingredients for which extension is sought; clear statement/illustration how such claims include items for approval/registration; ground for extension; number of days calculated for extension (capped at five years); date of approval; content of approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content of approval should detail items' number, firm name, drug name, dosage, efficacy/effect for drugs; registration number, firm name, name of agrochemical, type and content of active ingredient for agrochemicals; similar details for raw materials. Attach documents proving exclusive licensee/non-exclusive licensee/patent holder status if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation: scope and special power rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Special authorization is not required for representation of an application to register patent term extension; representation scope is determined by the scope of power of representation in the evidential document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the evidential document states broad scopes like 'all patent-related proceedings' and the representative's name is written in the application, the representative may handle subsequent proceedings. If representative's name is not written, representative may be deemed not to have power. Abandonment of the application requires special power of representation; without special power, the representative cannot abandon the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination procedure and timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure is similar to that for patent applications and is applied mutatis mutandis. Once received and transferred to an examiner, examination shall be initiated within four months from receipt of the application document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sequence: formalities examination by receiving division (or examiner if division fails), substantive examination (notify grounds for rejection and permit written arguments), submission of written arguments or amendment within designated period, re-examination considering amendments/arguments, decision to register or reject. If new grounds for rejection are found, notify and repeat the procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formalities defects handling
rubrics_metrics.description: If application violates formalities, examiner handles as prescribed: if filed after permitted period, notify intention to return, ground for return and allow period for explanation; if explanation not adequate, return documents. If representative provision violations, unpaid fees, or other formalities violations, examiner orders amendment within one month (extendable by one month). Failure to amend results in invalidation of the procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications filed before approval are treated in the same manner if they violate timing rules. Requests for return after notification or groundless explanations result in return of documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive statutory grounds for rejection (Article 91)
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner shall decide to reject an application where: 1) it is found unnecessary to obtain approval under Article 89(1) for practicing the patented invention; 2) the patentee/exclusive licensee/registered non-exclusive licensee fails to obtain approval under Article 89(1); 3) the length of extension applied exceeds the period during which the invention could not be practiced; 4) the applicant for registration is not the patentee; 5) the application is filed in violation of Article 90(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each ground is examined substantively and may trigger a written notice of ground for rejection allowing the applicant to respond or amend.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of necessity for approval — three core requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: To recognize a need to obtain approval under Article 89(1) for practicing the patented invention, the following must be met: ① approval is required for practicing (e.g., manufacturing/production) of the approved substance; ② the composition of the patented substance shall be identical with that of the approved substance (where invention is a substance); ③ the use of the patented substance shall be identical with the use of the approved substance (where invention is a use).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an approval body has approved an application for manufacturing items under the Pharmaceutical Affairs Act (e.g., to test activity/safety), the examiner may recognize that approval is required to manufacture the drug and may not further examine necessity unless special conditions (e.g., third party objection) exist. Examiner may request opinions from relevant organizations if unsure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of identicalness of composition
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the claim subject matter is a substance invention, the examiner shall compare the claimed substance and the approved substance. Where the claimed subject matter is a manufacturing-method invention, the examiner compares the substance manufactured by the disclosed method with the approved substance; manufacturing methods need not be compared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If compositions are not identical, the examiner shall deem it a ground for rejection under Article 91(1) and notify the applicant. The comparison focuses on the substance (or substance produced by claimed method) versus the approved product.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of identicalness of use (use inventions)
rubrics_metrics.description: For use inventions, the practicing of the patented invention refers to the use. If the use of the approved substance is not the same as the use disclosed in the patented invention, the patent term shall not be extended even if compositions are identical. However, if the patented use includes the approved use, the uses are deemed the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner must assess whether the claimed therapeutic/technical use covers the approved indications/uses; inclusion suffices for identicalness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of intermediates, catalysts, and manufacturing devices
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent rights relating to a manufacturing device for a final product, a catalyst used for manufacturing an intermediate or final product, or intermediates are not subject to extension of the patent term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: safety-regulating Acts (e.g., Pharmaceutical Affairs Act) govern manufacture and sale of final products, not intermediates. Therefore an extension based on approval of a final product cannot be used to extend patents directed to intermediates, catalysts, or manufacturing devices; examiner shall notify ground for rejection under Article 91(1)(1) if such an application is filed.
